tei_pid1_cumulative.command: docker exec rag-workbench-embedding-1 perl -e 'open(my $fh,"<","/proc/1/stat") or die "stat unavailable"; my @f=split(/\s+/,<$fh>); print "minflt=$f[9] majflt=$f[11] utime_ticks=$f[13] stime_ticks=$f[14] threads=$f[19]\n"; open(my $io,"<","/proc/1/io") or die "io unavailable"; while(<$io>) { print if /^(rchar|syscr|read_bytes):/; }'
tei_pid1_cumulative.caveat: Cumulative after startup and the preceding qualification; CPU/fault counters are not an isolated startup profile

cached_scattered_read_control.perl_probe: open(my $fh,"<",$ARGV[0]) or die "open failed"; binmode($fh); my $size=-s $fh; my $bytes=0; for my $i (0..4095) { my $at=(($i*104729)%int($size/4096))*4096; sysseek($fh,$at,0); my $count=sysread($fh,my $buffer,4096); die "read failed" unless defined($count); $bytes+=$count; } print "reads=4096 bytes=$bytes\n";
cached_scattered_read_control.command_template: docker exec rag-workbench-embedding-1 perl -e PROBE FILE; elapsed measured with PowerShell Stopwatch
cached_scattered_read_control.caveat: Already-cached samples; no meaningful Windows/Linux advantage observed in this microprobe

interpretation: A Linux-native cache is a justified experiment: mmap over 9p can incur page-fault overhead. Sequential read and cumulative counters do not prove the full startup cause; only a subsequent controlled model reload can establish the improvement.
